titre: The alphabet and spelling your name
intro: Many languages use the same 26 letters, but the English names of the letters are different: E sounds like “ee”, I sounds like “eye”. You need to spell your name, an email address or a word on the phone, at a hotel or in an office.
objectifs: Say the 26 letters of the English alphabet correctly.
Avoid the common confusions: E / I, G / J, A / R, H, W, Y.
Spell your name, your address and your email (double, capital, hyphen, dot, at).
Ask someone to spell a word and check information: How do you spell that?

texte: The easiest way is to learn the letters in groups with the same vowel. Each group rhymes: A, H, J, K rhyme with “day”; B, C, D, E… rhyme with “see”.
The letter Z is “zed” /zed/ in British English (and in Canada) and “zee” /ziː/ in American English.

lignes: B /biː/, C /siː/, D /diː/, E /iː/, G /dʒiː/, P /piː/, T /tiː/, V /viː/ (Z /ziː/ in the US)
F /ef/, L /el/, M /em/, N /en/, S /es/, X /eks/, Z /zed/ (UK)

texte: Some English letter names sound like a DIFFERENT letter in other languages. This causes most mistakes on the phone.

E is /iː/ (like “see”) and I is /aɪ/ (like “eye”). G is /dʒiː/ (like “gee”) and J is /dʒeɪ/ (like “jay”). A is /eɪ/ (like “day”) and R is /ɑː/ (like “car”). U is /juː/ (like “you”), and W is “double u”, not “double v”.
exemples: My name is Gilles: G-I-double L-E-S.
Say: gee, eye, double el, ee, es.

texte: For two same letters together, say “double”: double L, double S, double T (in American English, people often say the two letters: L-L).

Other words: capital (a big letter) or upper case; small letter or lower case; hyphen; apostrophe; space; accents: “e with an acute accent” (é), “e with a grave accent” (è). For an email: at (@), dot (.), underscore (_), dash or hyphen (-), slash (/).

lignes: capital M, small a, r, c
e acute / e with an acute accent
Hélène: H, e acute, l, e grave, n, e

exemples: My email is m.diallo@mail.com: M dot Diallo, D-I-A-double L-O, at mail dot com.

texte: To ask someone to spell: “How do you spell that?” / “How do you spell your surname?” / “Could you spell that, please?” (more polite). To check: “Sorry, could you repeat that?”; “Was that B or P?”; “Is that M for mother or N for night?”.

On the phone, people often say a word for a letter (“M for Mike, N for November”). Professionals use the international alphabet: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta, Echo, Foxtrot, Golf, Hotel, India, Juliett, Kilo, Lima, Mike, November, Oscar, Papa, Quebec, Romeo, Sierra, Tango, Uniform, Victor, Whiskey, X-ray, Yankee, Zulu.
exemples: How do you spell your name? — K-A-M-G-A.
Is that B for Bravo or P for Papa?
Could you spell that again, please?

texte: Many abbreviations are said letter by letter, with the English names of the letters: the UK /ˌjuː ˈkeɪ/, the USA, the EU /ˌiː ˈjuː/, a CV /ˌsiː ˈviː/, the BBC, a PC, an ID card /ˌaɪ ˈdiː/. The stress is on the last letter.
Remember (lesson 11): choose a / an by the sound of the first letter: an MP /em/, an FBI agent /ef/, a UN report /juː/.
exemples: Have you got an ID card?

formule: A /eɪ/ · E /iː/ · I /aɪ/ · O /əʊ/ · U /juː/ · G /dʒiː/ · J /dʒeɪ/ · R /ɑː/ · double L · capital · hyphen · at · dot
prononciation: Make E /iː/ (one long sound, lips spread) different from I /aɪ/ (two sounds, “a” then “i”).
G /dʒiː/ and J /dʒeɪ/ both start with /dʒ/ (as in “jam”); only the vowel changes.
H is /eɪtʃ/: don't forget the “tch” at the end. Some speakers say /heɪtʃ/.
W /ˈdʌbəljuː/ has three syllables: DOU-ble-you, stress on the first.
When you spell, make small groups of 3 or 4 letters with a pause. Your voice goes up at the end of each group except the last.
erreurs: In English, W is a “double u”.
How do you write your name? (asking for letters)
How do you spell your name?

dialogue.contexte: A customer calls a car rental office in Toronto to make a booking.
lignes: Good morning, City Car Rental. Can I have your name, please?
Sorry, how do you spell your first name?
H, E, L, E, N, E. With accents on the first two Es, but that's not important.
N, G, A, double S, A.
Yes, G for Golf. And my email is helene underscore ngassa at mail dot com.
Perfect, thank you. Your booking number is K7: K for Kilo, 7.
